items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: I'd tell J. C. Heard (he was our drummer during this period), "I'd like to do 'Limehouse Blues'. Follow me." And he did.

ctx.x: What kind of writing were you doing, or were you writing then?

No, I stopped writing after I left the band and the only kind of things I'd do were arrangements for myself and the only way I did them - you see, then musicians could really hear fast. On my way down the sound of the subway would bring me inspiration and I'd write an arrangement in my head before I got to the club and I'd tell J. C. Heard (he was our drummer during this period), "I'd like to do 'Limehouse Blues'. Follow me." And he did. If the musician was just great enough, anything you did they could follow.…
Did you have a bass and drums with you?
